query: Neues System: ein Händler-NPC, bei dem Spieler Materialien gegen Ausrüstung tauschen können. Leg los.
expected_behavior: Records the C++ boundary decision (classification, runtime truth, inspected existing seam, C++ versus asset ownership, count and justification of new native classes, asset work) before proposing code or assets.

Reuses existing seams after inspecting them, such as Lyra Interaction for talking to the merchant and the existing inventory transaction and cost logic for the exchange, instead of a parallel trade or inventory manager.

Keeps the authoritative exchange (validation, inventory mutation, replication) on the server in native code, and merchant stock, prices, NPC variants, text, and screens in DataAssets and CommonUI Widget Blueprints with MVVM.
Checks the request against the first-playable scope in `docs/game-vision.md`, where merchants are not MVP content, and proposes the smallest slice or asks whether to build it now.
Keeps trade truth out of the UI.

query: Plane ein Weltereignis-System: Portale öffnen sich zufällig in der Oberwelt, spawnen Gegnerwellen, zeigen eine UI-Warnung und geben beim Schließen Belohnungen.
expected_behavior: Splits the request into its systems (portal lifecycle and scheduling, spawning and AI, rewards, warning UI) and chooses the smallest verifiable slice, such as one portal encounter that spawns enemies and can be closed.
Records the C++ boundary decision: native lifecycle, authority, replication, and reusable scheduling; encounter variants, waves, rewards, visuals, cues, and tuning in feature assets.
Inspects and extends the existing portal actor, encounter component, and encounter definition in `Plugins/GameFeatures/GF_Portals_Core` instead of proposing a new manager.
Keeps the warning a Widget Blueprint that reflects replicated event state.
Flags drift toward a full Dungeonbreak or world-state simulation, which the vision defers beyond the first playable.
Reports the skills used, the chosen slice, and the remaining risks.

query: Das Testschwert soll 25 Prozent mehr Grundschaden machen.
expected_behavior: Treats the request as tuning of existing content, not as a new or extended system, and does not produce a C++ boundary decision or slice plan for it.
Finds where the sword's damage is actually defined (ItemDefinition, AbilitySet, GameplayEffect, or ability defaults) before changing anything.
Changes the value in that asset through the Unreal MCP workflow and adds no native class and no code constant.
Plans to validate the changed asset by saving and compiling or reloading it.
